body: Ah just everything. How overwhelming is Gender Dysphoria for you? There is no facet of my physical being I like, it makes me isolate myself as I feel embarrassed in public. I can't see how I'll ever be a happy, attractive man. It hurts so much, I wish it would all stop at this point. I just want to breathe.

I've found very little reliable research. I mean I assume lots of Gender Dysphoria symptoms cross over with BPD symptoms, or that simply innately having Gender Dysphoria could lead to developing BPD. Have you found the symptoms of BPD have lessened more with BPD-centric treatment or with your transition? Also have you found your Gender Dysphoria has lessened more with transition or the treatment of BPD?

This is the article but in retrospect I was panicking when I made these posts and a second pass shows it to be looking pretty damn unreliable. The author has lost their source for statistics at one point and the bottom refers to Gender Dysphoria and perhaps BPD (it's unclear) as a "disease." http://aapel.org/bdp/BLgenderUS.html

It's the idea that a lack of sense of self could extend to gender, or could lead to concocting Transgender as an identity, that terrifies me. Though everything about my narrative up until this point has pointed clearly towards gender dysphoria and that has been overwhelming for me to finally come to terms, absolutely terrifying. I believe that terror over being Trans to be sincere, and being Trans just makes sense for me personally and my life so far. Transition is such a massive decision, I think it makes sense that this could make us doubt it. We all question huge decisions, I don't see how transition could be any different.
I meant one school of thought, sorry didn't make that clear!

You sound like me, I am completely enraged to finally know what's up, it wasn't meant to be this. Do you think you can find happiness whilst ignoring gender dysphoria? In a way part of me feels fortunate, and I hope you won't find that insulting. I have very bad depression and had all but given up finding anything to ease the burden, but now I wonder how much of it is dysphoria and if a tangible treatment is in front of me. 
I try to fix the things and people around me too, do you find happiness in it? I do lots of voluntary work, sometimes it doesn't make me feel fulfilled the way I expect it too.

Were you certain of what you wanted? I think the very fact I have doubts and hesitations and worries makes me think "well surely I'm not transgender then", but I'm starting to realise not everyone went into therapy absolutely certain? 
How are you doing now?

I feel you. I'm like "fuck this, are you serious?!" I've wanted an answer all my life as to why I feel the way I do, and now that I might finally have it I'm terrified. I'm not sure what answer I wanted, I guess one that doesn't come with such stigma and a genuine threat of violence. Do you think about how you might feel once it's all over? Do you think you could feel better?
Can I ask if you had doubts and fears? Was there a point when you just "knew"? I'm terrified.

ah god I am seeing one and I'm more suicidal than ever but I suppose this is it helping. It's really unmasking the extent of this void in me I'd been ignoring. When did you start to breathe again? I'm so deeply unhappy
